prompt: Write a persistent builder whose add and addAll return NEW builders while the original keeps its old contents, and whose build() hands back an unmodifiable snapshot.
explanation: Persistent (immutable) data structures answer every change request with a new value instead of editing the old one, so an existing reference can never be changed underneath its owner. Copying this.items into a fresh ArrayList before appending is what makes that true, and passing the copy to the private constructor keeps the final items field assigned exactly once. Collections.unmodifiableList over a copy protects the snapshot in both directions: callers cannot add to it, and they cannot reach the builder's internal list through it.
hints: add and addAll start the same way: copy this builder's items into a brand new list, change the copy, and never touch the existing field.
Return new ImmutableListBuilder(next) -- that is what the private constructor is for.
build() should wrap a COPY, so use Collections.unmodifiableList(new ArrayList<>(this.items)).
